extracted.intended_audience: marketing, communications, and public relations professionals (PR pros, corporate communicators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and distributing effective press releases that attract attention from media, search engines, and stakeholders. Covers headline wording/length, overall release length and lead messaging, and timing of distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline relevance and conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: As the first thing the reader looks at (and one of the major elements search engines scan), your headline should be relevant and concise. Keep the character length to 88 characters or less, and include the most important keywords in the first 55 to 70 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the headline immediately informative and keyword-rich early; prioritize relevance and brevity because both human readers and search engines focus on the headline first. Avoid overly long or vague headlines that bury key terms past the 55–70 character mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall length and leading with 'why'
rubrics_metrics.description: The longer the press release, the less likely the reader is to read it in its entirety. For this reason, try to keep your press releases around 600 words, and lead with 'why' – as in, why should your audience care?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the most important messages up front to ensure readers get key information quickly and concisely. Treat verbosity as an anti-pattern; prioritize a strong lead that answers audience relevance and then provide supporting details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of distribution to stand out
rubrics_metrics.description: 52% of news is sent on the hour and half hour, with the highest volume of copy sent Tuesdays at 8:00 AM ET. Break the mold: Send your press releases at off times (like 8:47 AM ET) to stand out from the crowd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid predictable, high-volume distribution times if you want greater visibility. Use timing strategically to reduce competition for attention — small schedule offsets can help your release get noticed by journalists and news aggregators.
